 By Ira Winderman | iwinderman@sunsentinel.com | South Florida Sun Sentinel PUBLISHED: October 21, 2026 at 10:21 PM EDT | UPDATED: October 21, 2026 at 10:35 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... MIAMI — Observations and other notes of interest from Wednesday night’s 131-106 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves :
 – The defense was supposed to be the calling card.
 – And then, from the opening jump, it was the Timberwolves seemingly scoring at will.
 – So many defenders in the Heat’s opening lineup.
 – Such little defensive deterrence at the outset.
 – Which begs the question; is the Heat’s desire to play at pace coming at a cost of the defense?
 – Or is the goal to mesh both?
 – Even if it means stretches like at the outset of this one.
 – The roster says the Heat can defend.
 – Or at least should be able to defend.
 – The roster does not speak nearly as much to the offense.
 – Erik Spoelstra might want to have it both ways.
 – But is it coming at the cost of the best way?
 – Small sample size? Certainly.
 – But also a thought-provoking night.
 – There were no surprises with the Heat’s starting lineup, with the Heat opening with Bam Adebayo, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Andrew Wiggins, Davion Mitchell and Klay Thompson .
 – All three of the Heat’s two-way players were inactive: Tre Donaldson, Vlad Goldin and Keshad Johnson.
 – The Timberwolves opened with LaMelo Ball, Anthony Edwards, Jaden McDaniels, Jonathan Kuminga and Rudy Gobert.
 – Ball very much played as the engine sought.
 – Bobby Portis Jr. was first off the Heat bench.
 – Followed by Tim Hardaway Jr.
 – And, then, yes, Nikola Jovic was in the rotation, entered together with Pelle Larsson late in the opening period.
 – With Larsson playing as the de facto backup point guard.
 – That had Simone Fontecchio, Dru Smith and Nick Richards among those out of the initial mix.
 – Going in, Spoelstra said the goal was basic.
 – “Right now it’s just about, let’s get out there and compete,” he said pregame.
 – Of it being his 19th opening night as Heat coach, Spoelstra said, “That trips me up, how fast it’s gone.”
 – As for the group he brings into that 19th season, Spoelstra said, “I think it’s a group that really respects each other, respects what we’re trying to do, and look forward to connecting and getting together. That’s always a good thing. It helps, for sure, if you have a team that’s connected and enjoys each other’s company, eventually really enjoys and celebrates each other’s success.”
 – He added, “Those are the hallmarks of great teams. That doesn’t guarantee anything, but I think it’s more about everybody respecting what we feel is an opportunity.”
 – Spoelstra downplayed it being the first time Adebayo was on the court against Ball, after Ball’s injury-causing foul in last season’s play-in game in Charlotte.
 – “I said that, I don’t even need to say it now, he’s not a dirty player,” Spoelstra said of Ball. “That was a dirty play. That’s two separate things, but he’s an incredibly talented player.”

 – The Timberwolves became the 18th different opening-night opponent in the Heat’s 39 seasons.
 – The Heat entered 20-18 in season openers.
 – It was the eighth season-opening start for Adebayo. Dwyane Wade holds the franchise record of 12. The eighth start by Adebayo broke a tie with Udonis Haslem’s seven.
 – Adebayo entered 36 rebounds from breaking Haslem’s franchise career record.
 – Since the teams met a week ago in the preseason, the Timberwolves waived Antonio Reeves, Enrique Freeman, KJ Martin, Norchad Omier and Drew Timme.
 – Mario Chalmers was among the faces in the crowd.
 – As were Edgerrin James and Clinton Portis.
